note: Positions are a bearing and a range off the radar at Amarillo, projected here. Flare counts are per day, from the monthly operations report; the flight table gives none.

origin.name: the radar at Amarillo
origin.note: The flight tables give a bearing and a range and never say from where. Projected from Amarillo, 87% of the season's rows land inside the county their own row names; from the district office at White Deer, 9%. Whether the bearings are true or magnetic is not stated, and no rotation is applied: as printed, 76.5% of releases land in the county their row names, against 93.8% for West Texas and 96.1% for Trans-Pecos, the two programmes that print coordinates in one form all season. About 6° of eastward rotation closes most of that gap, which is what a magnetic display would mean — 4 km at 30 nm, about a 3 km cell. South Texas projects its radials from an origin inferred the same way and wants about the same six degrees, which is the only corroboration there is. `positions.mjs` is where those figures come from.
